To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hydrogen peroxide can be detected in the pulpal chamber following vital bleaching treatment and this amount is significantly increased when heat is applied along with the H2O2.

1) the application of heat with H 2 O2 significantly increases H 2 O penetration into the pulp, 2) the application of H 2O2 at higher concentrations (10 and 30%) also increases the amount of H 2 that reaches into the pulp, and 3) the application of 1% H 2O at 37deg C did not result in any measurable penetration into the pulp.

the amount of hydrogen peroxide that reaches the pulp chamber is directly related to the concentration of the hydrogen peroxide solution, and that the amount of uptake can be increased by the use of heat.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of bleaching agents on the pulp chamber, and it is concluded that the pulp is not protected from bleaching agents by dentin.
the penetration of H 2 0 2 into the pulp chamber during vital bleaching procedures and the effects that temperature and time may have on this process.
the effects of bleaching on pulp tissue and its ability to penetrate into the dentin tubules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amount of H 2O 2 reaching the pulp during vital bleaching is minimal and that the application of heat enhances the penetration.
H 2 O2 is capable of penetrating the pulp chamber and reaching the pulp tissue during vital bleaching procedures.
the application of heat along with the 30% H2O2 bleaching agent will cause the greatest amount of pulp chamber penetration and therefore, the greatest amount of damage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amount of H 2 0 2 in the pulpal chamber is dependent on both the concentration of H 2O 2 and temperature.
H 2 O2 does penetrate the pulp and the extent of penetration is enhanced by the application of heat.
the amount of H 2O2 that reaches the pulpal tissues is significant, but not enough to cause irreversible pulpal damage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
H 2 O2 can be absorbed into the dentin and reach the pulp chamber.
vital bleaching treatments can be performed safely if the H 2O 2 concentration is maintained below 10%.
